title: Airspeed Unreliable
ref: QRH NNC 10.1 (NG & MAX) · PI Flight With Unreliable Airspeed

flash.title: Climbing through FL140, night, IMC, icing.
flash.text: Captain's airspeed levels off while the F/O's decreases, A/T in N1. Captain-side stick shaker activates, yet pitch and thrust are normal for the climb.

steps.item: Set the following gear up pitch attitude and thrust: Flaps extended
Set the following gear up pitch attitude and thrust: Flaps up

trap: Trusting the stick shaker or overspeed warning: they can sound falsely, even simultaneously. Pitch + N1 first, analyze later.
then: Reliable indications: Attitude, N1, Ground speed, Radio altitude
Reliable airspeed identified? → use it for the rest of the flight (reliable-side F/D ON, reliable-side A/P if needed, no A/T)
Otherwise: PI table “Flight With Unreliable Airspeed”, stabilized and trimmed, compare all 3 airspeeds: deviation > 20 kt or 0.03 M = unreliable
Altitude unreliable on both sides → not RVSM, transponder ALT OFF
diff: Memory items identical NG/MAX. The MAX NNC adds notes: the Stick Shaker Indicator on the AOA indicator (and the AOA readout/pointer/approach band if AOA is the cause) may be unreliable; on NG the AIRSPEED LOW alert is “(as installed)”.

qcm.q: Flaps up: which pitch / N1 memory item?
qcm.w: Flaps up: 4° and 75% N1. 10°/80% is for flaps extended, still gear up.

qcm.q: Flaps extended (gear up): which pitch / N1?
qcm.w: Flaps extended: 10° and 80% N1, per NNC 10.1, NG and MAX alike.

qcm.q: What is the 3rd memory item?
qcm.w: Order: A/P Disengage → A/T Disengage → F/D (both) OFF → pitch/thrust. PROBE HEAT is the first reference item, after the dashed line.

qcm.q: Which indication is NOT listed as reliable by the QRH?
qcm.w: Reliable: Attitude, N1, Ground speed, Radio altitude. Stick shaker, overspeed and AIRSPEED LOW may sound falsely.

qcm.q: Stabilized with the PI table, an airspeed is considered unreliable if it differs by more than…
qcm.w: “differs by more than 20 knots or 0.03 Mach from the airspeed shown in the table”.

sources.quote: Flaps extended . . . 10° and 80% N1 / Flaps up . . . 4° and 75% N1
3 F/D switches (both) . . . OFF
The following indications are reliable: Attitude N1 Ground speed Radio altitude
An airspeed indication that differs by more than 20 knots or 0.03 Mach from the airspeed shown in the table should be considered unreliable.
The Stick Shaker Indicator on the Angle of Attack indicator may be unreliable.
The last immediate action item is followed by a dashed horizontal line.

title: Runaway Stabilizer
ref: QRH NNC 9.1 (NG & MAX) · FCTM ch.8 Runaway Stabilizer / Manual Stabilizer Trim

flash.title: Cruise FL350, A/P engaged.
flash.text: The trim wheel spins continuously, the trim clacker never stops. Column forces build and pitch drifts while airspeed is stable.

steps.action: Control airplane pitch attitude and airspeed

steps.item: If the runaway stops after the autopilot is disengaged:
steps.action: Do not re-engage the autopilot or autothrottle.

steps.item: If the runaway continues after the autopilot is disengaged: STAB TRIM cutout switches (both)
If the runaway continues: Stabilizer trim wheel

nums.s: MAX: STS (Speed Trim + MCAS) inhibited, SPEED TRIM FAIL

trap: Disengaging the A/P without holding the column: you lose the A/P elevator commands. Hold the column firmly BEFORE disconnecting. Once off, do not re-engage A/P or A/T.
then: Stabilizer … Trim manually (two-pilot effort may be used)
Reducing airspeed reduces manual trim forces
Anticipate trim needs, do not re-engage A/P or A/T
Deferred items: landing configuration and in-trim established early on final
diff: Memory items identical NG/MAX (QRH 9.1). System differences: on MAX the cutouts are STAB TRIM PRI and B/U and disconnect A/P, main electric and Speed Trim System (Speed Trim + MCAS); on NG they are MAIN ELECT and AUTOPILOT. On MAX, pulling the column does not stop an MCAS nose-down trim.

qcm.q: First Runaway Stabilizer memory item?
o: Stabilizer trim wheel … Grasp and hold
qcm.w: Hold the column firmly before disconnecting the A/P to keep pitch control and retain the A/P elevator commands (FCTM).

qcm.q: A/P disengaged, runaway continues. Action?
qcm.w: “If the runaway continues after the autopilot is disengaged: STAB TRIM cutout switches (both) … CUTOUT”.

qcm.q: Cutouts set, stab still moving. Action?
o: Stabilizer trim wheel … Grasp and hold
qcm.w: “If the runaway continues: Stabilizer trim wheel … Grasp and hold”. Grasping the trim wheel stops stab movement (FCOM).

qcm.q: Runaway stops as soon as the A/P is disengaged. Next?
o: Do not re-engage the autopilot or autothrottle
Cutouts to CUTOUT as a precaution
qcm.w: “If the runaway stops after the autopilot is disengaged: Do not re-engage the autopilot or autothrottle.”

qcm.q: On MAX, what does a STAB TRIM cutout (PRI or B/U) at CUTOUT disconnect?
o: A/P, main electric and Speed Trim System (Speed Trim + MCAS)
qcm.w: FCOM MAX: A/P, main electric and STS (Speed Trim and MCAS) inputs are disconnected from the trim motor. The manual trim wheel remains available.

sources.quote: 1 Control column . . . Hold firmly 2 Autopilot (if engaged) . . . Disengage
If the runaway continues after the autopilot is disengaged: STAB TRIM cutout switches (both) . . . CUTOUT If the runaway continues: Stabilizer trim wheel . . . Grasp and hold
8 Stabilizer . . . Trim manually A two-pilot effort may be used to correct an out of trim condition.
The control column must be held firmly before the autopilot (if engaged) is disengaged to maintain airplane pitch control and retain any elevator commands from the autopilot.
One unit of stabilizer trim requires approximately 15 turns of the stabilizer trim wheel.
If either switch is positioned to CUTOUT, the autopilot, main electric and Speed Trim System (Speed Trim function and MCAS function) trim inputs are disconnected from the stabilizer trim motor.
If the left and right AOAs disagree by 5.5 degrees or more with the flaps retracted, the SPEED TRIM FAIL light illuminates
The STAB TRIM MAIN ELECT cutout switch and the STAB TRIM AUTOPILOT cutout switch, located on the control stand

title: Emergency Descent
ref: QRH NNC 0.1 (NG & MAX) · SOP B737 Ed03 Rev03

flash.title: FL370, cruise.
flash.text: Cabin can no longer be controlled after the CABIN ALTITUDE WARNING NNC: masks at 100%, crew communication established. Decision: immediate rapid descent.

steps.action: The pilot flying will advise the cabin crew, on the PA system, of impending rapid descent. The pilot monitoring will advise ATC and obtain the area altimeter setting.
descend to the lowest safe altitude or 10,000 feet, whichever is higher.
Reduce thrust to minimum or as needed for anti-ice
(Caution: If structural integrity is in doubt, limit speed as much as possible and avoid high maneuvering loads.)

nums.s: or lowest safe altitude, whichever is higher

trap: Descending to 10 000 ft without checking MSA: it's the higher of lowest safe altitude and 10 000 ft. And with structural doubt, don't chase Mmo/Vmo.
then: Approaching level-off: SPEED BRAKE lever DOWN, level off, add thrust
Crew oxygen regulators … Normal (O2 mandatory above 10 000 ft cabin altitude)
New plan based on weather, oxygen, fuel, airports (LRC possible)
SOP: recommended technique A/P in LVL CHG, A/T engaged, no V/S; F/O calls 2 000 and 1 000 ft before level-off
diff: Same items. Lever label is “SPEED BRAKE” on MAX, “Speedbrake” on NG. QRH NG (YD101–YD105) caution: speedbrake autostows to the 50% flight detent above 320 kt if GW > 70 308 kg; do not counter the autostow unless below 320 kt.

qcm.q: Emergency descent target altitude?
o: FL100 or MSA, whichever is lower
Lowest safe altitude or 10 000 ft, whichever is higher
qcm.w: “descend to the lowest safe altitude or 10,000 feet, whichever is higher”.

qcm.q: Per the QRH, who announces the descent to the cabin on the PA?
qcm.w: PF advises the cabin on the PA; PM advises ATC and obtains the area altimeter setting.

qcm.q: ENGINE START switches in the memory items?
qcm.w: “ENGINE START switches (both) … CONT”.

qcm.q: Structural integrity in doubt: speed?
o: Limit speed as much as possible, avoid high maneuvering loads
qcm.w: QRH caution: limit speed as much as possible and avoid high maneuvering loads.

qcm.q: On some heavy NGs (YD101–YD105), the speedbrake may…
o: Autostow to 50% flight detent above 320 kt
qcm.w: QRH NG caution: GW > 70 308 kg, autostow to the 50% flight detent if airspeed exceeds 320 kt.

sources.quote: 3 Without delay, descend to the lowest safe altitude or 10,000 feet, whichever is higher.
6 SPEED BRAKE . . . FLIGHT DETENT ... 7 Set target speed to Mmo/Vmo.
6 Speedbrake . . . FLIGHT DETENT
When gross weight is greater than 70,308 kgs, speed brake will autostow to the 50% flight detent if airspeed exceeds 320 knots.
use of the autopilot with LVL CHG mode is the recommended technique for rapid descents. Use of the V/S mode is not recommended.

title: Warning Horns (Landing / Takeoff Configuration)

flash.title: Lined up on the runway, setting takeoff thrust.
flash.text: As the thrust levers are advanced for takeoff, an intermittent horn sounds and TAKEOFF CONFIG illuminates. Later, on final, a steady horn…

steps.item: If in flight, the steady warning horn sounds (LANDING CONFIGURATION):
If the intermittent warning horn sounds or a CABIN ALTITUDE light illuminates in flight at an airplane flight altitude above 10,000 feet MSL:
steps.action: Don the oxygen masks and set the regulators to 100%. Establish crew communications. ►►Go to the CABIN ALTITUDE WARNING or Rapid Depressurization checklist

steps.item: If the intermittent warning horn sounds or a TAKEOFF CONFIG light illuminates on the ground when advancing the thrust levers to takeoff thrust:

nums.s: ground = TO config · flight > 10 000 ft = cabin
if intermittent horn in flight > 10 000 ft MSL

trap: Mixing up the two horns: in flight above 10 000 ft MSL, the intermittent horn is a cabin altitude warning → masks first, not a configuration check.
then: On the ground (thrust levers advanced to takeoff thrust): establish correct takeoff configuration before any departure
Intermittent horn > 10 000 ft MSL: CABIN ALTITUDE WARNING or Rapid Depressurization (QRH 2.1)
Steady horn in flight: establish correct landing configuration
diff: Identical items. On NG, the TAKEOFF CONFIG and CABIN ALTITUDE lights are “(if installed and operative)”; on MAX they are always fitted (Captain and F/O Main Panels).

qcm.q: In flight, STEADY horn. Memory item?
qcm.w: LANDING CONFIGURATION: “In flight, the steady warning horn sounds” → Assure correct airplane landing configuration.

qcm.q: In flight at FL250, INTERMITTENT horn. First action?
o: Don the oxygen masks and set the regulators to 100%
qcm.w: Above 10 000 ft MSL, intermittent = cabin altitude: masks at 100%, crew communication, then NNC 2.1.

qcm.q: On the ground, thrust advanced, intermittent horn. Memory item?
qcm.w: TAKEOFF CONFIGURATION: Assure correct airplane takeoff configuration.

qcm.q: After masks and crew communication for an intermittent horn in flight, which NNC?
o: CABIN ALTITUDE WARNING or Rapid Depressurization
qcm.w: “►►Go to the CABIN ALTITUDE WARNING or Rapid Depressurization checklist on page 2.1”.

qcm.q: Airplane altitude above which the intermittent horn becomes a cabin altitude warning?
qcm.w: “in flight at an airplane flight altitude above 10,000 feet MSL”.

sources.quote: In flight, the steady warning horn sounds. 1 Assure correct airplane landing configuration.

sources.loc: NNC 15.2 WARNING HORN (INTERMITTENT) or WARNING LIGHT - CABIN ALTITUDE OR TAKEOFF CONFIGURATION
sources.quote: Don the oxygen masks and set the regulators to 100%. Establish crew communications.
TAKEOFF CONFIG light (if installed and operative) illuminates when advancing the thrust levers to takeoff thrust: Assure correct airplane takeoff configuration.
